plan: Store a deep copy of the input dictionary in the constructor and return deep copies from to_data(), isolating internal state from callers.
Provide one recursive traversal generator yielding (item, parent_list, index, depth) that all query and move operations share.
Compile two regexes: one matching marker tokens [[?identifier]] (capturing the identifier) and one matching words \b\w+\b; strip markers from note text before counting words.

Compute total_word_count() by summing marker-stripped word counts of notes and declared word_count of references; compute unresolved_markers() by unioning note marker identifiers with reference unresolved lists, returned sorted.
Render outline() as the workspace title followed by one line per item in traversal order, indented two spaces per nesting depth, formatted as '<kind>: <title>'.

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: check both ids are strings, locate the moved item and the destination container ('workspace' literal or a section/group), verify the destination is a container, the index is within 0..len(destination), and the destination is neither the item nor inside its subtree; only after all checks pass, pop the item from its parent list and insert it into the destination, so any failure leaves the tree byte-for-byte unchanged.
mechanisms: defensive deep copying at the construction and export boundaries
single recursive generator as the shared traversal primitive
compiled regex pair for marker extraction and marker-free word counting
set-based accumulation with lexicographic sort for unresolved marker identifiers
depth-indexed string building for the deterministic outline
full-precondition validation before mutation (atomic move with pop/insert)
recursive subtree membership check to reject self- and descendant-containment
